extracted.intended_audience: early-career faculty applying for NSF CAREER (Faculty Early Career Development) awards and NSF peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Review criteria for NSF Faculty Early Career Development (CAREER) program proposals, emphasizing intellectual merit, broader impacts (with added weight for educational leadership), integration of research and education, PI qualifications, project plan and resources, and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Encompasses the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the two National Science Board-approved merit review criteria used to evaluate CAREER proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Encompasses the potential to benefit society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the two National Science Board-approved merit review criteria. For a CAREER Award, the broader impacts criterion carries extra weight because the program explicitly values educational leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to advance knowledge and benefit society (Five Elements #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential to advance knowledge (Intellectual Merit) and benefit society (Broader Impacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly listed as the first of five elements of evaluation for CAREER proposals; overlaps with the two standard merit review criteria but is restated as a central evaluative element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity, originality, and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the project ideas are novel and could lead to significant shifts or advances in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of project plan and assessment mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the plan for carrying out proposed activities is well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on sound rationale with mechanisms to assess success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on the coherence and feasibility of the approach and whether the proposal includes means to measure and demonstrate progress or outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the PI
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual to conduct the proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider the PI's background, prior work, and potential to execute the proposed research and education activities successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and institutional environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are adequate resources available to carry out the proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes availability of facilities, equipment, institutional commitments, and other resources necessary for project execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Research and Education
rubrics_metrics.description: The defining feature of a CAREER proposal is the integration of research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect a cohesive plan where: (1) Research activities inform educational activities; (2) Educational activities inform research activities; (3) The PI articulates a coherent vision for their academic career; (4) Plans extend beyond the typical 5-year award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental/Institutional Endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of institutional support and commitment to the PI's career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for departmental/institutional evidence such as the department's commitment to the PI's career development and a mentoring plan from senior faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent career development plan (CAREER-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the CAREER plan as a coherent integrated career trajectory rather than two separate proposals (research + education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal should present an integrated trajectory tying research and educational goals into the PI's broader academic career vision.
